claim: The Route des Crêtes (D141) is about 17 km between Cassis and La Ciotat, peaking at La Grande Tête at 399m, and features the Pont Naturel arch, the Dent du Chat, and a Semaphore (1791) at 349m.
quote: La Grande Tête – 399m ... Le Pont Naturel, a natural arch carved out by erosion ... Dent du Chat, an astonishing stone arch ... Semaphore, which dates back to 1791 and stands at an altitude of 349m

claim: The D141 along Cap Canaille is roughly 15km long, reaches 394m, has the highest sea cliffs in France, is drivable in 30min (allow 1hr for viewpoints), has free car parks, should be avoided in high wind, and is pedestrianised every Sunday.
quote: the D141 road along the cliffs is about 15 kilometres long ... reach an altitude of 394 metres ... the highest sea cliffs in France ... All car parks are free ... should be avoided when there are high winds ... pedestrianised every Sunday

claim: Cap Canaille is among the highest sea cliffs in Europe; the Route des Crêtes is closed on very windy days, is pedestrian-only every Sunday in season, and parking at viewpoints is limited so arriving early is advised.
quote: at 363m, it is the highest sea cliff in Europe! ... When it's very windy, the road is closed ... from April 28 to September 29, 2024, the Route des Crêtes will be pedestrian-only every Sunday

claim: Cassis SNCF station is 3km from the town centre with a shuttle bus, taxis or a 40-minute walk; trains from Marseille arrive roughly every 30 minutes, and bus 78 links Marseille to Cassis every 45 minutes.
quote: located 3 km from the town centre ... a dedicated shuttle bus, taxis, or a 40-minute walking route ... From Marseille, trains arrive approx. every 30 minutes ... Route 78 connects Marseille to Cassis every 45 minutes

claim: Bus 373 from the free Gorguettes park-and-ride costs €1.70 round trip (€0.80 per trip on a reloadable ticket, under-6s free); summer brings overcrowding and peak-hour road closures, and on a red fire-risk day land access is banned and the Route des Crêtes closes while boat visits remain possible without landing.
quote: take bus 373 from the free park-and-ride parking lot of Gorguettes ... €1.70 round trip ... In case of a "red day," the access to the Calanques National Park is forbidden by land, the "route des Crêtes" is closed, but the visit by boat remains possible with any landing strictly forbidden

claim: The Relais des Gorguettes is a free 220-space park-and-ride with a free shuttle serving the centre of Cassis and Port-Miou, recommended when central car parks are saturated.
quote: The Gorguettes parking lot is free with 220 spaces, and a free shuttle serves the center of Cassis and Port-Miou

claim: From 1 June to 30 September the Calanques massif is regulated daily by colour-coded fire risk (green/orange/red); on red days land access is banned and the Route des Crêtes is closed, with status updated daily at 6pm and checkable via the 'Mes Calanques' app or by phone.
quote: access bans to the National Park from 1 June to 30 September on days classified as 'red' ... using the official "Mes Calanques" mobile application. The status updates daily at 6pm

claim: Cap Canaille is one of the highest sea cliffs in Europe at 394m at La Grande Tête; the 15km Route des Crêtes can close at any time without notice on windy days, and summer access follows the same massif fire regulations.
quote: one of the highest cliffs in Europe, falling on the sea (394 meters high at the level of the Grande Tête) ... on windy days in particular, the Route des Crêtes can be closed at any time and without notice
